title: Merging touching daily windows removed 14 of 41 multiple-RI storm labels in Atlantic HURDAT2 in 1982-2025
abstract: We tested how daily-window grouping changes repeated rapid intensification (RI) labels in Atlantic HURDAT2 in 1982-2025. There were 201 RI storms among 657 eligible storms. Consecutive six-hour qualifying starts gave 41 storms with multiple episodes. Merging connected 24-hour windows, including touching windows, left 27. The removed fraction was 34.1%, with a conditional 95% three-year block interval of 19.4% to 50.0%. Merging only strict overlap removed eight labels, or 19.5%. Short gaps between qualifying starts explain the count difference. Both rules gave uncertain era changes. This is a catalog definition test, not a count of separate physical pulses or a climate trend result. One release, wind rounding, land exposure and resampling assumptions limit inference. Code, aggregate evidence, hashes, retrieval instructions, an interval-graph audit and a figure are included. Source and storm records remain external.

display.caption: Merging daily RI windows removes multiple-episode labels. Left: fractions removed with conditional 95% three-year block intervals. Right: multiple fractions among RI storms in two equal eras. Neither era-change interval excludes zero.
